name: Sumo Squat
description: The sumo squat uses a significantly wider stance than a conventional squat with the toes pointed outward at approximately 45°. The wide stance shifts the loading emphasis toward the inner thigh adductors and gluteus maximus, while reducing the range of motion required at the ankle. It is accessible to those with limited ankle dorsiflexion and provides a unique adductor stimulus absent from standard squatting variations. It can be performed with a dumbbell, kettlebell, or barbell.

execution.starting_position: Stand with feet much wider than shoulder-width, toes pointed out 30–45°. Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically with both hands between the legs if adding load.
execution.setup_instructions: Foot width depends on hip structure and mobility — start with feet twice shoulder-width and adjust. Toes should point in the same direction as the knees.
steps: Step 1: Stand with wide stance, toes pointed out. Hold weight if applicable. Core braced.
Step 2: Descend by pushing the knees out in line with the toes while sitting the hips directly down.
Step 3: Descend until the thighs are parallel to the floor. The wide stance allows the torso to remain upright.
Step 4: Drive through both feet to return to standing, squeezing the glutes and inner thighs at the top.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale before descent. Exhale as you return to standing.
common_mistakes: Knees caving inward (valgus) during descent — actively push knees out over the toes
Leaning excessively forward despite the wide stance — the sumo squat should allow a more upright torso
Feet positioned so the toes point further out than the knees
safety_considerations: Ensure hip external rotator flexibility before using a very wide stance
If knees are painful in the wide-stance position, reduce foot width
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Aim for parallel or below while keeping the spine neutral. The wide stance often allows greater depth without lumbar rounding.
coaching_cues: Knees track over the pinky toe
Drop straight down — don't let the torso pitch forward
Squeeze the glutes and inner thighs to stand
